pr_body:
# ↪️ Pull Request

This adds support for React Refresh, the successor of react-hot-loader.
Closes #3499

(AFAICT, create-react-app doesn't have this by default and there are currently multiple competing webpack plugins. I'm not aware of any web bundler implementation that correctly implements this like Metro)

A syntax error, and errors thrown during module initialization or render cause only the parent to rerender

Add charset to the dev server's headers to prevent the emoji in the HMRRuntime (`🚨`) from becoming `ðŸš¨`.

## 🚨 Test instructions

Running the `example/react-refresh` example, changing some component reloads that component while the random numbers at the top (local state) don't change.
This also works after a syntax error was created and resolved.

## 🗣  "Slightly controversial decisions"

- What babel parser options should a transformer use if it doesn't want to deal with the users babel config? Maybe we should create a utility function for that.
   - asset.meta.babelPlugins ?

issue_context.title: Support Fast Refresh for React
issue_context.body:
Fast Refresh is a new hot reloading implementation for React that's first-class and doesn't have weird semantic quirks present in userland solutions. We first implemented it for RN, but integrating it on the web needs some work in the bundlers.

If you're interested in adopting it for Parcel, I wrote down first thoughts on how it could be done: https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/16604#issuecomment-528663101. This should be something you can reasonably expect to prototype in a few hours. There's a much more in-depth discussion on nuances to happen afterwards but I'd be happy to help steer that work and answer questions. Thanks for consideration!

Are we sure these functions aren't supposed to do something?

Yes, every asset has a prelude, where there hooks are set to an actual implementation, and a postlude, where they are set to their previous values (like a stack). So the function at the very bottom has to be defined.
Metro does this and Dan also put this into his implementers guide.

But if the AST from the JSTransformer was reused, then JSTransformer#generate is never called?
Mmm, yeah. This is annoying. We should possibly rethink how parsing/generating works. Maybe a separate “parser” plugin type would be useful to centralize this.
Maybe use the memory fs for input instead. Should be more reliable on Windows if possible.
